note.explanation: Network security protects data and networks from unauthorized access and attacks. Firewalls monitor and control network traffic, encryption makes data unreadable without the correct decryption key, and passwords and authentication help ensure that only authorized users can access network resources.
examples: A firewall can block unwanted network traffic.
A shift cipher changes “Hello” to “Khoor” by moving each letter three places down the alphabet.
note.checkAnswer: A firewall monitors and controls network traffic according to security rules.
note.simple: Network security is like protecting a house: a firewall is the gatekeeper, encryption is a secret code, and a password helps check who is allowed in.
note.title: Network Security
steps: Use a firewall to monitor and control incoming and outgoing network traffic.
Encrypt sensitive data so that only someone with the correct decryption key can understand it.
Use passwords and authentication to check that users are authorized.
Watch for threats such as malware, phishing, DoS attacks, and man-in-the-middle attacks.
note.answer: Network security uses measures such as firewalls, encryption, and authentication to protect data and prevent unauthorized access to networks.

written.text:
Q6.8. Consider a shift cipher with a shift amount of 4.
(a) Encrypt the message "SECURITY".
(b) Decrypt the message "WMXYVMI".

rubric.why: The encryption must begin by applying the stated shift forward to the letters.
rubric.description: Show or correctly apply the forward shift of four places.
rubric.how: Shift each plaintext letter four positions down the alphabet.

rubric.why: The encrypted message must be correct.
Decryption must reverse the shift used for encryption.
rubric.description: Show or correctly apply a backward shift of four places.
rubric.how: Shift each ciphertext letter four positions back in the alphabet.

rubric.why: The decrypted message must match the given ciphertext and shift.

modelAnswer: (a) Shift each letter of SECURITY four places down the alphabet.
S → W, E → I, C → G, U → Y, R → V, I → M, T → X, Y → C
(b) Shift each letter of WMXYVMI four places back in the alphabet.
W → S, M → I, X → T, Y → U, V → R, M → I, I → E

examTips: A short question may ask you to explain encryption or the role of a firewall. Give the definition and then state how it protects a network or data.
A long question may ask you to discuss security methods. Explain each method separately and finish by comparing how they protect against different threats.
For a shift-cipher question, show the shift for each letter and write the complete encrypted or decrypted message clearly.
Use precise terms such as ciphertext, decryption key, authorized users, incoming and outgoing traffic, and predetermined security rules.

hints: For encryption, move each letter forward in the alphabet.
For a shift of 4, map each letter of SECURITY four places down the alphabet.

explain.title: Why network security matters
explain.body: Network security involves measures to protect data and prevent unauthorized access to computer networks. It helps protect sensitive data, defend against attacks, maintain privacy, and keep network resources available to authorized users.

explain.title: Firewalls
explain.body: Firewalls are security systems that monitor and control incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined security rules. They act as barriers between trusted internal networks and untrusted external networks.

explain.title: Encryption and decryption
explain.body: Encryption transforms data into a secure format that can only be read or understood by authorized parties with the correct decryption key. Decryption is the process of converting the encrypted data back to its original form.

explain.title: Passwords and authentication
explain.body: Passwords and authentication methods ensure that only authorized users can access network resources. Strong passwords help protect access to those resources.

explain.title: Common threats
explain.body: Malware is malicious software that can damage or steal data. Phishing uses deceptive emails or websites to trick users into revealing sensitive information. DoS attacks overwhelm a network with traffic, while man-in-the-middle attacks intercept communication between two parties.

mistakes: Do not confuse encryption, which changes data into a secure format, with decryption, which changes it back to its original form.
Do not say that a firewall encrypts data; its stated function is to monitor and control network traffic.
When using a shift cipher, do not shift one way for both encryption and decryption: decryption reverses the shift.
Do not forget to use the correct decryption key when explaining who can read encrypted data.
Do not describe phishing as malware: phishing is an attempt to trick users into revealing sensitive information.
